t: This is Berners Street, running north of Oxford Street in the West End. It began in the mid-eighteenth century as a residential street, developed by William Berners, and the street carries his name. He was a property developer and a slave owner, and he is closely linked with the development of Fitzrovia, the area north of Oxford Street. Later the street filled with larger commercial and semi-industrial buildings and mansion blocks of flats. It was home to makers of pianos, harps and furniture, and to film-makers. Charles Dickens is also associated with it.
